resources.string: You\'re protected. Review this any time.
Android won\'t ask again. Open settings, then allow it under Permissions.
Eldering uses your precise location to know where an accident happened and to show you on the map to the people you choose. Choose \"Precise\" and \"While using the app\".
Eldering uses your location in the background

Eldering collects location data even when the app is closed or not in use, to:
• detect accidents and falls while you walk or drive,
• keep your last hour of trail on this phone for "Trip to past",
• share your live location with the family members you allow, and send your location if an accident is detected or you hold SOS.

Your trail stays on this phone. It is uploaded only during an accident or SOS and deleted from the server after 72 hours. You can pause or turn off sharing at any time.
On the next screen, choose \"Allow all the time\". Without it, Eldering can\'t help while your phone is in your pocket.
Lets Eldering tell walking from driving, so it uses the right accident checks and saves battery while you\'re still.
The \"Are you OK?\" countdown and your family\'s accident alerts arrive as notifications.
If an accident is detected, Eldering texts your emergency contacts your location, even without mobile data. It never texts anyone else and never places calls.
Lets the accident countdown fill the screen even when your phone is locked. On the next screen, allow full-screen notifications for Eldering.
Android may pause apps to save battery. Allow Eldering to keep running so it can notice an accident at any time. It is built to use little battery.
OnePlus phones can stop safety apps in the background. Please do these three things once:
Open App info → Battery and choose \"Allow background activity\" (or \"Don\'t optimize\").
Open Recent apps, tap the menu on Eldering\'s card and choose \"Lock\".
